text:
ConocoPhillips fell 4.7% today as crude oil prices collapsed more than 7%, driven by diplomatic developments suggesting potential U.S.-Iran negotiations could ease Middle East tensions and reduce supply disruption risk. When oil prices drop sharply, the revenue and earnings outlook for oil producers like ConocoPhillips contracts immediately, and investors sell shares accordingly. The move was particularly steep because it reversed a strong rally just two trading days earlier, when the stock had jumped 2.7% to $154.03.

The sharp reversal also reflects how sensitive energy stocks are to geopolitical risk premiums embedded in oil prices. As long as conflict risks in the Middle East remain in play, oil commands a price "cushion" that benefits producers; the moment peace talks gain credibility, that cushion deflates rapidly. The current disconnect between U.S. oil ($103/barrel) and world oil ($123/barrel) underscores how much regional tensions still matter to global pricing.
